key_insight: Sequential evaporation does not convert wide-bandgap and narrow-bandgap perovskite stacks the same way, so bandgap control must be tailored to the specific solid-state conversion pathway.
engineering_relevance: This enables solvent-free fabrication of all-perovskite tandem solar cells with a 1.26-1.96 eV absorber range, culminating in a first evaporated tandem device at 19.2% efficiency.
method: Time-sliced ex situ analysis of sequentially evaporated precursor stacks
Compare solid-state conversion in mixed-halide WBG versus Sn-Pb NBG absorbers
Use bandgap-guided absorber design for tandem device fabrication
evidence_signal: The paper reports a first evaporated all-perovskite tandem solar cell with 19.2% power conversion efficiency and 80% average retained efficiency after 1,200 h at 65 °C (ISOS-D-2).
watch_item: Conversion is highly pathway-dependent, so uncontrolled precursor thickness, diffusion, or annealing conditions may create vertical compositional gradients and shift the final bandgap.
paper_title: Divergent Solid-state Conversion Pathways in Evaporated All-perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
